question: What is a scalar ?
expected_context: Scalars: A scalar is just a single number, in contrast to most of the other objects studied in linear algebra, which are usually arrays of multiple numbers. We write scalars in italics. We usually give scalars lowercase variable names.
expected_answer: A scalar is just a single number, in contrast to most of the other objects studied in linear algebra, which are usually arrays of multiple numbers.

question: What is a tensor ?
expected_context: Tensors: In some cases we will need an array with more than two axes. In the general case, an array of numbers arranged on a regular grid with a variable number of axes is known as a tensor.
expected_answer: A tensor is an array of numbers arranged on a regular grid with a variable number of axes. We use it when we need an array with more than two axes.

question: What is an identity matrix ?
expected_context: An identity matrix is a matrix that does not change any vector when we multiply that vector by that matrix. The structure of the identity matrix is simple: all the entries along the main diagonal are 1, while all the other entries are zero.
expected_answer: An identity matrix is a matrix that does not change any vector when we multiply that vector by that matrix. All the entries along its main diagonal are 1, while all the other entries are zero.
